dimensions.assessment: Affects Indian Tribes, tribal organizations, Bureau of Indian Affairs law enforcement, federal law enforcement agencies, and Native communities.
dimensions.evidence: establishing a grant program for specified entities (e.g., tribes) to implement changes to enhance their responses to missing person cases

dimensions.assessment: Aims to improve investigative coordination, data collection, background check processing times, and mental health support for tribal and BIA law enforcement.
dimensions.evidence: ensure that federal training resources and culturally appropriate mental health and wellness programs are available to tribal and Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) law enforcement officers

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes appropriations of $1,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030 for the missing or murdered response coordination grant program.
dimensions.evidence: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out the grant program... $1,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

dimensions.assessment: Requires multiple federal agency actions, new reporting mandates, a 5-year BIA background check demonstration program, and GAO studies.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of the Interior shall establish a five-year demonstration program for the purpose of conducting or adjudicating personnel background investigations

dimensions.assessment: Includes multi-year grant authorizations through 2030 and a 5-year sunset provision for the BIA background check demonstration program.
dimensions.evidence: The demonstration program established under paragraph (1) shall terminate 5 years after the date of the commencement of the demonstration program.

importance_detail.rationale: The BADGES for Native Communities Act addresses missing and murdered Indigenous persons by appointing NamUs Tribal facilitators, requiring detailed law enforcement personnel resource reports, establishing a BIA background check demonstration program, creating a response coordination grant program, and coordinating officer counseling resources.

label: H.R. 1010

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini. (rated before the current eligibility rules; kept)

summary: The BADGES for Native Communities Act revises federal policies and procedures to improve information sharing, reporting, and investigations regarding missing, unidentified, or murdered Indigenous persons. The bill establishes Tribal facilitators, grant programs, background check demonstration programs, interdepartmental wellness coordination, and Government Accountability Office studies.

affected_groups.effect: Tribes and tribal organizations may apply for grants, receive technical assistance, coordinate on missing persons cases, and participate in background check and data-sharing agreements.
Officers receive access to culturally appropriate mental health and wellness programs, and applicants face a new five-year background check demonstration program.
affected_groups.group: BIA and Tribal Law Enforcement Officers

affected_groups.effect: Federal agencies face new annual reporting requirements on personnel resources, time spent in Indian country, vacancy rates, and a GAO study on evidence collection and response procedures.
affected_groups.group: Federal Law Enforcement Agencies (BIA, FBI, DOJ)

key_provisions: Requires the Attorney General to appoint National Missing and Unidentified Persons System (NamUs) Tribal facilitators to coordinate reporting, provide technical assistance, and maintain communication with Indian Tribes.

Establishes a five-year demonstration program for the Department of the Interior to conduct or adjudicate personnel background investigations and security clearances for Bureau of Indian Affairs law enforcement applicants.

Requires the Attorney General to establish a grant program within the Office of Justice Programs for tribes, tribal organizations, and states in consortium with tribes to support missing or murdered response coordination activities.

Requires the Government Accountability Office to conduct a study on the evidence collection, handling, response times, and processing procedures of federal law enforcement agencies like the BIA and FBI.

Requires the Department of Health and Human Services and the Attorney General to coordinate with the BIA to ensure federal training materials and culturally appropriate mental health and wellness programs are available to BIA and tribal law enforcement officers.
Expands reporting requirements regarding unmet staffing, infrastructure, and technology needs for tribal and bureau justice agencies.
missing_information: The total overall cost of the legislation, aside from authorizing $1,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2026 through 2030 for the grant program, is not specified.
Specific details on the exact outcomes or future reauthorization thresholds beyond the initial reporting periods and the 5-year demonstration sunset are not fully detailed.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The BADGES for Native Communities Act revises federal policies and procedures to improve information sharing, reporting, and investigations regarding missing, unidentified, or murdered Indigenous persons. The bill establishes Tribal facilitators, grant programs, background check demonstration programs, interdepartmental wellness coordination, and Government Accountability Office studies.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation addresses systemic data gaps, investigative hurdles, and resource needs surrounding missing and murdered Indigenous persons across Indian country. The law impacts federal and tribal justice administration, background check processing times, inter-agency coordination, and reporting transparency.

title: BADGES for Native Communities Act
